The [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") ([Swedish](Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Nobelpriset i fysiologi eller medicin*) is awarded annually by the Swedish [Karolinska Institute](Karolinska_Institutet "Karolinska Institutet") to scientists in the various fields of [physiology](Physiology "Physiology") or [medicine](Medicine "Medicine"). It is one of the five [Nobel Prizes](Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") established by the 1895 [will](Will_(law) "Will (law)") of [Alfred Nobel](Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel") (who died in 1896), awarded for outstanding contributions in [chemistry](Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry"), [physics](Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"), [literature](Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature"), [peace](Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize"), and physiology or medicine.[[1]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physiology_or_Medicine#cite_note-1) As dictated by Nobel's will, the award is administered by the [Nobel Foundation](Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") and awarded by a committee that consists of five members and an executive secretary elected by the Karolinska Institute.[[2]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physiology_or_Medicine#cite_note-2)[[3]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physiology_or_Medicine#cite_note-History-3) While commonly referred to as the Nobel Prize in Medicine, Nobel specifically stated that the prize be awarded for "physiology or medicine" in his will. Because of this, the prize can be awarded in a broader range of fields.[[3]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physiology_or_Medicine#cite_note-History-3) The first Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded in 1901 to [Emil Adolf von Behring](Emil_Adolf_von_Behring "Emil Adolf von Behring"), of Germany. The award is presented in <Stockholm> at an annual ceremony on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[5]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physiology_or_Medicine#cite_note-5)
